dispositions.rationale: The spec decides this trade-off: ACE-D4 makes a rule-and-site citation a mechanical detection, ACE-D5 makes the owner's labels on calibration items the check on false ones, and ACE-A56 refuses a calibration holding no mechanical detection. Judging every detection would change the decision, not fill a gap.

The repeat cap and the retest are one planning decision, what the planner plans next for a run, delivered by one slice and not acceptable apart; ACE-A19 holds the scorer's side of the repeat limit. Splitting yields two criteria that cannot be delivered independently.

A parent pass is a fold over its cases' locks, not a separate obligation: ACE-A49 names every unlocked case, and the thresholds and the no-averaging rule parameterise the one lock decision ACE-A52 states.

Artifact placement is what the slice list fixes: S2.2 and S2.5 place the check and the documents under evals/, the merged check reads the manifest beside itself, and the S2.5 continuation requires the committed catalogue to pass it. A criterion observing a path proves no behaviour.
Repeats prior obligation-reduction-3, whose rationale holds: The installer suite holds test_eval_corpora_never_deploy_for_any_tool, which fails when any skill evals/ directory reaches a staging plan.

Repeats prior obligation-reduction-1, whose rationale holds: One sentence is the authoring form of the detection statement, which the judge reads whole; no scored behaviour depends on its sentence count.

Repeats prior obligation-reduction-2, whose rationale holds: The source revision is provenance; a harvested document is edited to plant its defect, so nothing in the tree can compare it with the revision, and the owner reads it at validation.

The sentence states why the form is duplicated; a criterion observing where the form lives is an implementation prescription, and the restraint rule earns it no criterion. The form's observable effect is which IDs the check reads off ACE-D3's table, which ACE-A12 exercises and the evidence sidecar now cites for a digit-prefixed ID and a hyphen-continued one.

Operator-observed. Repeats prior obligation-reduction-13, whose rationale holds: Writing the plan before dispatch rests on the operator, as the decision states; nothing in the committed tree can observe it. The tree-observable part, the record's report, decision, digests and acceptance, is ACE-A13.

Repeats prior obligation-reduction-7, whose rationale holds: The judge identity the record can hold is its resolved model ID and prompt digest, which ACE-A20 checks; the invocation path is not observable in a committed record.
Repeats prior obligation-reduction-13, whose rationale holds: Writing the plan before dispatch rests on the operator, as the decision states; nothing in the committed tree can observe it.
Repeats prior obligation-reduction-14, whose rationale holds: Committing every attempt rests on the operator, as the decision states; nothing in the committed tree can observe it.
Tracker-observed. Repeats prior obligation-reduction-20, whose rationale holds: The verification child is a tracker item the human closes under ACQ-D2; the tree cannot observe the tracker.

The content-tests target discovers every suite under src/ by name, so a suite the slices place under evals/ cannot sit outside the gate; the criteria themselves are behavioural. Repeats prior obligation-reduction-21, whose rationale holds: The gate clause in a continuation line is the delivery contract gate the work facade requires there, not a criterion of this spec.
Repeats prior obligation-reduction-21, whose rationale holds: The gate clause in a continuation line is the delivery contract gate the work facade requires there, not a criterion of this spec.

Repeats prior obligation-reduction-21, whose rationale holds: The gate clause in a continuation line is the delivery contract gate the work facade requires there, not a criterion of this spec.

No circumstance makes ACE-A23 and ACE-A24 unsatisfiable together: a newly added case has a fingerprint with no attempt, so ACE-A21 admits a baseline attempt on it under the earlier template, after which both lock sets cover the same cases and ACE-A23 compares them. ACE-D9 asks for a whole-catalogue comparison, which presupposes a baseline covering the catalogue.

ACE-D5's sentence sets a necessary condition and grants no permission, so the scorer refuses a record that meets it without contradiction; ACE-A56 states which items count as new. Repeats prior what-if-2, whose rationale holds: A record calibrating a prompt digest an earlier record failed is refused; ACE-D5 recalibrates only after revision.

ACE-A67 decides it: the scorer writes nothing, so its report is output, which the traceability table's check column accepts; no sentence requires the report to be committed, and it is regenerable from the committed runs.

The document decides this failure path: a planned run with no usable report after two repeats leaves its case pending and the evaluation incomplete (ACE-A19), never a miss, and ACE-D8's serialisation rule targets an attempt with no committed reports. A planner refusal is not what the document implies.

parts.statement: The manifest and case documents occupy the prescribed evals locations.
Evaluation cases never deploy.

obligations.source: ACE-D2: 'Cases live in src/user/.claude/skills/ac-attack/evals/, so they never deploy.' It places documents under 'evals/cases/<id>/'.
obligations.statement: Evaluation cases occupy the prescribed repository tree and never deploy.

parts.statement: Required manifest fields are present, and catalogue identity, served parents, rule, lens and child match the fixed table.
A duplicate manifest key makes the manifest unusable.
Each detection statement consists of one sentence.
A harvested document's recorded source revision identifies its source.

obligations.source: ACE-D2 lists the ID, served parent criteria, rule, lens, defect site, 'a one-sentence detection statement' and 'the source revision of any harvested document'; 'a key written twice makes it unusable'.
obligations.statement: The manifest supplies the prescribed case metadata without ambiguous keys.

parts.statement: The fixed catalogue uses the prescribed criterion IDs from ACE-D3's table.
The case checker contains its own definition of the specified criterion-ID form and edge semantics.

obligations.source: ACE-D2: 'a prefix of upper-case letters and digits, a hyphen, the letter A and digits, bounded by the lint's ID edges rather than word boundaries'; 'The case check holds its own copy of that form'.
obligations.statement: Criterion IDs use the lint-defined form, and the case checker owns an independent copy of that definition.

parts.statement: Pair documents are present, readable, distinct, differ in one contiguous hunk and match their validation digests; their lens enforces their rule.
Control-only cases contain no defective document or site, and unreadable present documents do not evade that restriction.
The committed catalogue is usable as accepted input to the prescribed case-check interface.

obligations.source: ACE-D2 requires defective.md and control.md differing 'in one contiguous hunk', with no defective document or site for a control-only case. S2.5 delivers 'The documents in evals/cases/', each in ACE-D2's format.
obligations.statement: Case documents have the prescribed pair or control-only structure and are usable by the case checker.

parts.statement: Before counted runs, the required control or panel run and complete owner review establish the intended defect, correction and parent no-finding feature, with upheld additional defects amended.
The checker refuses unreadable or duplicate-key validation records, missing reports, decisions or digests, non-acceptance decisions, and documents differing from accepted digests.

obligations.source: ACE-D2: 'the owner validates a case before its runs count'; the lens runs over the control and the owner 'reads every objection', confirms the parent's Given and no-finding feature, and amends pairs carrying another upheld defect. A control-only case receives 'one panel run, read whole'. The record holds the report, decision and digests.
obligations.statement: Cases receive substantive owner validation before their runs count, and retain a document-bound validation record.

parts.statement: A catalogue lacking a case for a standard rule is refused with the rule named.
Missing listed cases and departures from the fixed parent, rule, lens or child mappings are refused with the case named.

obligations.source: ACE-D3: 'The catalogue follows the parent's own text'; its table specifies each case's served parents, rule, lens and child. The introduction assigns each rule exactly one owning lens.
obligations.statement: The catalogue covers the standard's rules and contains the cases and ownership mappings fixed by the parent-derived table.

obligations.source: ACE-D3's catalogue identifies C1–C29 and P1. ACE-D7 defines locking, ACE-D8 defines the evaluation of record as current locks, and S2.7 requires every case to hold a current lock.
obligations.statement: Every fixed evaluation case obtains a current lock under the stated finite evaluation contract.

parts.statement: Configuration, isolation and planned-count mismatches are refused and named; repeats do not inflate the planned count.
An unavailable transport cannot yield a counted substitute or a completed evaluation without usable reports.

obligations.source: ACE-D4: 'A run is one fresh dispatch of one lens over one document.' ACE-D6 specifies transport, model, effort and Reads; 'A run on a substituted model or effort does not count. A down transport means the evaluation waits.'
obligations.statement: Counted lens runs use the production configuration and prescribed isolation.

parts.statement: Detection uses the rule/site and judge-match cases exactly, including sites of none.
A control is non-silent only for a relevant rule/site objection judged to describe the detection statement.
Empty reports are counted separately from silent reports for the empty-control rate.
A P1 panel passes only when all four lens runs contain no judged demand for implementation criteria.

obligations.source: ACE-D4 defines mechanical and judged detection, control silence, reports marked empty, and four-run P1 panel success.
obligations.statement: The scorer distinguishes detection, silence, empty reports and P1 panel success as specified.

parts.statement: No third repeat is planned.
Unresolved reports or judgments leave the case pending, excluded from rates, with an incomplete evaluation reported.

obligations.source: ACE-D4: missing or wholly malformed reports are repeated 'at most twice'; unresolved reports or judgments leave the case pending; 'A pending case is never scored as a miss.'
obligations.statement: Unusable reports receive bounded repeats, and unresolved reports or judgments leave the case pending and evaluation incomplete.

parts.statement: Judgments use Claude Opus through the native Agent tool with evals/judge.md.
Assembled judge inputs contain exactly the prescribed case or P1 information and no lens, model or arm information.

obligations.source: ACE-D5: 'The judge is Claude Opus through the native Agent tool, with the prompt evals/judge.md.' Case tasks receive rule text, detection statement and one objection; P1 receives one objection. 'It never sees the lens, the model or the arm.'
obligations.statement: The prescribed judge receives only the permitted task information.

parts.statement: Uncalibrated tasks, insufficient agreement, non-owner labelling and model or prompt mismatches are refused with a reason.
Failed prompts cannot be recalibrated unchanged, failed calibration items cannot be reused, and case-task calibration includes mechanical detections.
Judgment records bind the run to its calibrated model and prompt, and comparisons use one judge model and prompt.

obligations.source: ACE-D5 requires Scott Hamilton to label twenty items, eighteen agreements, revised prompts and twenty new items after failure, mechanical detections in case-task calibration, and calibration of experiment tasks in the same way. Records name the labeller, items, prompt digest and judge model ID.
obligations.statement: Judgments count only under the specified owner-labelled calibration and recorded judge identity.

parts.statement: Detection and control sides pass at the specified five-run and ten-run counts and fail at the other counts.
Only sides at three of five receive a retest, and all ten runs count.
Cases require both sides; P1 uses its specified panel thresholds; parents require all serving cases; scoring uses planned thresholds and averages no rate across cases.
Each lens's empty-control rate pools its current-lock control runs, including its P1 runs, and passes only at at least 80 percent with a nonempty pool.

obligations.source: ACE-D7 fixes four of five, the three-of-five retest and eight of ten, joint detection/control locking, P1 thresholds, every-case parent acceptance and the 80-percent pooled empty-control threshold.
obligations.statement: Case, side, parent and empty-control acceptance use the fixed thresholds without discarding runs or averaging case rates.

parts.statement: Reports state pooled detection and silence rates and name every unlocked case with its failing or pending side.

obligations.source: ACE-D7: 'The scorer also reports each lens's pooled rates, which decide nothing.' The What-if questions say a failure names the failing case.
obligations.statement: The scorer reports descriptive pooled rates and identifies unsuccessful cases.

parts.statement: Plans and usable reports agree on cases, dispatch counts, configuration and thresholds; plans above 310 dispatches require named owner approval.
Attempt plans precede all dispatches and retest extensions precede retest dispatches.

obligations.source: ACE-D7 refuses plans larger than 310 dispatches without owner approval, experiments included. ACE-D8 requires a plan 'before any dispatch' and a retest extension 'before the retest', fixing dispatches, configuration, thresholds and cases.
obligations.statement: Plans fix the dispatches and evaluation parameters in advance and respect the approved dispatch budget.

parts.statement: Every attempt and all its reports, including failed and superseded reports, are retained and committed under the prescribed run directory.

obligations.source: ACE-D8: 'Every attempt is committed with its reports under evals/runs/<run-id>/, whatever it shows'; 'A repeat's superseded reports stay committed and match nothing.'
obligations.statement: All attempt evidence is retained and committed regardless of outcome.

parts.statement: The scorer reads the served model from transport metadata and refuses configuration mismatches.
Usable reports match planned attempt and retest runs one to one; absent or duplicate response IDs are refused; superseded reports match nothing.

obligations.source: ACE-D8 requires transport response metadata, the served model and response ID, model lookup from the response, one-to-one planned-run matching and refusal of duplicate response IDs.
obligations.statement: Usable report provenance and dispatch matching are checked mechanically.

parts.statement: Document and emitted-prompt changes void exactly the locks whose prompt bindings changed, including changes affecting a P1 lens prompt.
The recorded fingerprint itself includes the prescribed model and effort.

obligations.source: ACE-D8 defines fingerprints from emitted document prompts 'with ACE-D6's model and effort', including all four P1 prompts. A lock is current while its fingerprint matches; changes void only affected locks.
obligations.statement: Locks bind to their producing prompts and configuration, and changes invalidate exactly the affected locks.

parts.statement: Stored reports are rescored without planned lens dispatch, and locks survive only if their cases still pass.

obligations.source: ACE-D8: a judge prompt, judge model or scorer change 'dispatches no lens'; stored reports are rescored and a lock stands only when the case still passes.
obligations.statement: Judge or scorer changes reuse stored lens reports and retain only locks that still pass.

parts.statement: Repeated attempts on an already attempted fingerprint and attempts blocked by uncommitted planned reports are refused and identified.

obligations.source: ACE-D8 gives a fingerprint one attempt plus its earned retest, refuses another attempt whether locked or failed, and refuses new attempts while a planned attempt has no committed reports.
obligations.statement: A fingerprint cannot be rerolled, and incomplete planned attempts block new attempts.

parts.statement: Improvement requires every baseline lock to survive and gains in at least two lenses; failures identify regression or missing gain.
Comparisons reject differing configurations, judges, prompts or case sets and pending cases.
The template gate binds the current digest to a registry chain beginning at the pinned constant, with reproducible improving comparisons from committed lock sets and whole-catalogue coverage.

obligations.source: ACE-D9 requires preservation of all baseline locks and gains in at least two lenses, reserves one-lens gains for that lens's prompt, and defines the committed lock-set comparison chain, initial constant and current-template digest test.
obligations.statement: Shared-template additions require a reproducible, comparable whole-catalogue improvement recorded in the digest registry.

parts.statement: A baseline attempt on every case is committed.
Every revised lens has a lens-level comparison naming no regressed case.

obligations.source: S2.6: 'A baseline attempt on every case, then body revisions ... each shown by a lens-level comparison to regress no case.' The corresponding unnumbered continuation criteria are identified here as CONT-S2.6-BASELINE and CONT-S2.6-NO-REGRESSION.
obligations.statement: Lens-mandate work establishes a committed baseline for every case and demonstrates no regression for each revised lens.

parts.statement: The verification child cannot close while any required case lacks a current lock.

obligations.source: S2.7: 'It stays open until every case holds a current lock.'
obligations.statement: The verification child remains open until the evaluation evidence is complete.

parts.statement: The promised evaluation suites and registry test are delivered, with the stated suites included in make content-tests.

obligations.source: S2.2 promises check_cases.py 'with its suite'; S2.3 promises the planning, scoring and judge artifacts and 'their suites'; S2.4 promises comparison mode and 'the registry test'. The acceptance-section introduction says the emitter and checker suites run under make content-tests.
obligations.statement: The evaluation helpers ship their promised suites and registry test through the stated test entry point.

parts.statement: The case checker, scorer and comparison return the same answers without writes on unchanged inputs; a repeated attempt request is refused without a second plan.

obligations.source: The What-if questions state: 'Every check is a read, so running it twice or with nothing changed answers the same way.' ACE-D8 permits only one attempt per fingerprint.
obligations.statement: Repeated unchanged checks are deterministic and read-only, and repeated planning creates no second plan.

ground.reason: ACE-D2 assigns each case a detection statement. ACE-D5 explicitly acknowledges that an objection can cite the correct rule and site while describing something else. Nevertheless, ACE-D4 automatically counts that objection as a detection. ACE-A25 requires only a current C1 lock, checked through the scorer's report. Calibration checks a separate sample; it does not validate these automatically counted objections.

objections.objection: ACE-A25 can pass when the lens never identifies C1's planted defect.
objections.obligation: Detect the defect represented by C1's detection statement.

scenario.expect: The scorer records five detections and five silent controls, locks C1, and passes ACE-A25, although none of the defective-run objections describes the planted defect.
scenario.given: A validated C1 pair, valid calibration and dispatch records, five defective reports whose objections cite C1's rule and site but describe an unrelated problem, and five empty control reports.
scenario.when: The scorer applies ACE-D4 and ACE-D7 and reports the evaluation of record.

ground.reason: ACE-A46 combines retest eligibility, a maximum report-repeat count, and scoring all ten retained runs. ACE-D7 supplies the retest and scoring promises; ACE-D4 supplies the repeat limit. Planning a statistical retest, limiting malformed-report retries, and scoring the retained sample can each be delivered and accepted independently. The traceability table assigns their combined verification to the scorer suite and report.

objections.objection: ACE-A46 places three independently acceptable results under one acceptance decision.

scenario.expect: ACE-A46 passes, while retest eligibility, the repeat limit, and retained-run scoring have no separate acceptance decisions.
scenario.given: A deliverable that correctly schedules eligible retests, refuses third repeats, and scores every retested side using all ten runs.
scenario.when: The suite verifies all three behaviours and records the single ACE-A46 result.

ground.reason: ACE-A52 combines case-lock decisions, parent acceptance, use of the plan's fixed thresholds, and a prohibition on averaging rates across cases. ACE-D7 promises case locking, parent acceptance, and separate case rates; ACE-D8 promises scoring under the planned thresholds. Parent acceptance and threshold selection can be accepted or rejected independently of case locking. The named scorer-suite and scorer-report checks do not separate these acceptance obligations.

objections.objection: ACE-A52 bundles independently deliverable scoring and closure obligations into one criterion.

scenario.expect: ACE-A52 passes, while parent closure, threshold selection, and the prohibition on cross-case averaging have no acceptance decisions independent of case locking.
scenario.given: A scorer that correctly locks pair and P1 cases, requires every serving case before passing a parent, uses planned thresholds, and keeps rates separate across cases.
scenario.when: The fixture suite checks these results and records one ACE-A52 verdict.

ground.reason: ACE-D2 says cases live in the specified evals tree. The checks cover catalogue contents and scoring, but do not establish that location.

objections.objection: The evaluation can pass with its case documents stored outside the promised repository location.

scenario.expect: Every criterion passes, but the case documents are absent from src/user/.claude/skills/ac-attack/evals/cases/.
scenario.given: A valid catalogue and validated case documents are stored elsewhere and supplied to the evaluation helpers.
scenario.when: The catalogue checks, evaluation and comparisons run.

ground.reason: ACE-D2 promises that cases never deploy. No criterion observes deployment exclusion.

objections.objection: Evaluation cases can deploy while all evaluation criteria pass.

scenario.expect: Every criterion passes, but deployed skill content includes evaluation cases.
scenario.given: The evaluation catalogue is valid and locked, but deployment copies its evals directory.
scenario.when: The evaluation criteria run and the skill is deployed.

ground.reason: ACE-D2 says a manifest key written twice makes the manifest unusable. ACE-A13 rejects duplicate keys in validation records, but does not require the same rejection for the manifest.

objections.objection: A manifest containing duplicate keys can be accepted.

scenario.expect: Every criterion passes, but the case check accepts the duplicate-key manifest.
scenario.given: cases.json repeats a key with the same value, and the parser silently retains its last occurrence.
scenario.when: The case check and evaluation run.

ground.reason: ACE-D2 requires a one-sentence detection statement. ACE-A13 checks that the manifest field exists, but no criterion checks this content constraint.

objections.objection: Detection statements can violate the promised one-sentence format.

scenario.expect: Every criterion passes, but a detection statement contains several sentences.
scenario.given: All manifest fields are present and a multi-sentence detection statement describes the intended defect correctly.
scenario.when: Validation, scoring and comparison run.

ground.reason: ACE-D2 requires the source revision of any harvested document. Field presence does not establish that the recorded revision identifies the harvested source.

objections.objection: A harvested case can carry incorrect source provenance.

scenario.expect: Every criterion passes, but the manifest names a revision from which the document was not harvested.
scenario.given: A valid harvested pair has the correct validation digests but an unrelated source revision in its manifest.
scenario.when: The case check and evaluation run.

ground.reason: ACE-D2 explicitly requires the case check to hold its own copy of the lint's criterion-ID form and ID-edge semantics. Matching the fixed catalogue table does not establish that constraint.

objections.objection: The checker can omit the promised independent criterion-ID definition.

scenario.expect: Every criterion passes, but the checker contains no independent definition of the specified ID form and edges.
scenario.given: The checker compares catalogue metadata with hardcoded table entries and implements the other required checks.
scenario.when: The specified catalogue and scoring checks run.

ground.reason: ACE-D2 requires validation before runs count, including the control run, the owner's complete review and confirmation of the parent's defect and no-finding feature. ACE-A13 establishes the validation record's structure and acceptance, but not that this procedure occurred.

objections.objection: Cases can count without the required substantive validation.

scenario.expect: Every criterion passes, but a counted case has not received the required complete control review and content confirmation.
scenario.given: A pair has valid documents, digests and an acceptance record, but the owner accepts it without reading every control objection or checking the parent's Given and no-finding clauses.
scenario.when: The case check accepts the record and the case obtains a current lock.

ground.reason: ACE-D5 fixes the judge as Claude Opus through the native Agent tool using evals/judge.md. Calibration and model-ID consistency do not establish that prescribed dispatch route.

objections.objection: A judge dispatched through another transport can satisfy the criteria.

scenario.expect: Every criterion passes, but judgments are obtained without the native Agent tool.
scenario.given: The same calibrated Opus model and judge prompt are invoked through another transport, with matching recorded model IDs and prompt digests.
scenario.when: Judgments are produced and the evaluation is scored.

ground.reason: ACE-D8 requires the attempt plan before any dispatch and its retest extension before the retest. The criteria check plan contents and scoring against them, but not their creation order.

objections.objection: Plans can be written after the runs they purport to prescribe.

scenario.expect: Every criterion passes, but dispatches precede their committed plan or retest extension.
scenario.given: The operator performs the required runs, then writes plans containing the correct counts, cases, configuration and thresholds.
scenario.when: Reports are committed and the planner and scorer checks run.

ground.reason: ACE-D8 requires every attempt and its reports to be committed whatever they show, and explicitly retains superseded repeat reports. ACE-A53 excludes superseded reports from matching; it does not require their retention.

objections.objection: Superseded reports can disappear from the committed evaluation evidence.

scenario.expect: Every criterion passes, but the committed attempt omits its superseded reports.
scenario.given: A run returns an unusable report and a permitted repeat returns a usable report. Only the usable report is retained and committed.
scenario.when: The scorer checks one-to-one matching and the catalogue obtains its locks.

ground.reason: ACE-D8 says the fingerprint includes ACE-D6's model and effort. ACE-A47 samples document and emitted-prompt changes, while configuration checks do not require those values to be included in the fingerprint itself.

objections.objection: Lock fingerprints can omit the prescribed configuration binding.

scenario.expect: Every criterion passes, but fingerprints contain prompt digests without model and effort.
scenario.given: Runs use the correct configuration and lock sets record it separately, but the fingerprint implementation hashes only emitted prompts.
scenario.when: The specified prompt-change, scoring and comparison checks run.

ground.reason: S2.7 says the verification child stays open until every case holds a current lock. Its continuation criteria observe the eventual evaluation result, not premature closure.

objections.objection: The verification child can close before its required evidence exists.

scenario.expect: Every criterion eventually passes, but the verification child was closed while a case remained unlocked.
scenario.given: The verification child is closed after implementation, before the evaluation finishes.
scenario.when: The remaining cases later obtain current locks and the final criteria are checked.

ground.reason: The ordered slices promise the case-check, planning, scoring and comparison suites and registry test. Successful gate exit alone does not establish that these deliverables exist or are included in the gate.

objections.objection: The promised suites can be missing from the delivered evaluation tooling.

scenario.expect: Every criterion passes, but a promised suite is absent or omitted from make content-tests.
scenario.given: The helpers satisfy the behavior checks through an external verification harness, while make content-tests runs only the existing unrelated tests.
scenario.when: The behavior checks and continuation gates run.

ground.reason: No text outside the criteria independently promises the content-tests exit status. The S2.2 gate criterion observes that status, which does not establish the promised checker behavior or suite delivery.

objections.objection: The S2.2 gate criterion discharges no inventoried obligation.

scenario.expect: The gate exits 0 while no independent document obligation depends on that exit status.
scenario.given: The case-check obligations are assessed separately and content-tests can pass without running its promised suite.
scenario.when: The S2.2 continuation runs make content-tests.

ground.reason: The S2.3 gate's exit status does not establish planning, scoring, judging or delivery of their suites. The document supplies no separate obligation about that status.

objections.objection: The S2.3 gate criterion discharges no inventoried obligation.

scenario.expect: The gate exits 0 while no independent document obligation depends on that exit status.
scenario.given: The S2.3 behavior checks are assessed separately and content-tests runs only unrelated tests.
scenario.when: The S2.3 continuation runs make content-tests.

ground.reason: The S2.4 gate's exit status does not establish comparison semantics or registry enforcement. The document supplies no separate obligation about that status.

objections.objection: The S2.4 gate criterion discharges no inventoried obligation.

scenario.expect: The gate exits 0 while no independent document obligation depends on that exit status.
scenario.given: Comparison and registry behavior are assessed separately and content-tests omits their promised tests.
scenario.when: The S2.4 continuation runs make content-tests.

ground.reason: The S2.5 gate's exit status does not establish catalogue content or substantive validation. The document supplies no separate obligation about that status.

objections.objection: The S2.5 gate criterion discharges no inventoried obligation.

scenario.expect: The gate exits 0 while no independent document obligation depends on that exit status.
scenario.given: Catalogue acceptance and evaluation are assessed separately and content-tests runs unrelated tests.
scenario.when: The S2.5 continuation runs make content-tests.

ground.reason: ACE-A24's registry check requires an entry's improves report to be reproducible by the comparison from the two named lock sets, yet it demands full catalogue coverage only of the later set. In the circumstance where the earlier set covers fewer cases (a case added to the catalogue between the two attempts), ACE-A23 makes the comparison refuse those two sets, so the report ACE-A24 requires can never exist. Both criteria apply to the same registry entry and demand incompatible verdicts.

objections.objection: A template addition whose baseline lock set predates a catalogue growth is unregistrable: ACE-A24 fails the emitter suite because ACE-A23 guarantees the comparison refuses the only lock sets the entry can name, so no genuine improvement can ever ship through the gate ACE-D9 defines.
objections.obligation: ACE-D9's template gate: an addition ships only with a whole-catalogue comparison reporting improves, recorded as a registry entry the emitter suite verifies.

scenario.expect: ACE-A24 requires a reproduced improves report from the named sets, but ACE-A23 requires the comparison to refuse them for differing in the cases they cover; the suite fails and the T1 addition cannot be registered no matter how strong its evidence.
scenario.given: A committed registry whose last entry is template T0, a baseline lock set produced under T0 covering the catalogue as it then stood, a new catalogue case C-new added afterwards, and a candidate template T1 whose later lock set covers every catalogue case including C-new while the earlier set does not.
scenario.when: The emitter suite checks the new registry entry naming those two lock sets under ACE-A24, and the comparison is asked to reproduce the entry's improves report under ACE-A23.

ground.reason: ACE-D5 says a prompt that failed calibration is calibrated again only after revision, on twenty new items — read as new relative to the failed calibration being answered. ACE-A56 refuses any calibration record that shares an item with a failed calibration of any earlier prompt digest. When a revised prompt answers a later failure using items that an unrelated earlier failed calibration used, ACE-D5 permits the record and ACE-A56 refuses it; both apply to the same record.

objections.objection: An owner following ACE-D5's recalibration rule can produce a calibration record the scorer must refuse: the criterion lets through no reading in which 'twenty new items' means new only against the failure being answered, yet that is the reading ACE-D5's text most naturally carries.
objections.obligation: ACE-D5's calibration rule: a failed prompt is calibrated again only after revision, on twenty new items.

scenario.expect: ACE-D5's recalibration rule is satisfied (revision, twenty items not used in the failed calibration being answered), but ACE-A56 refuses the record because it shares items with v1's failed calibration of an earlier prompt digest; the run cannot be scored.
scenario.given: Prompt digest v1 failed calibration on items 1–20; its revision v2 passed on items 21–40; a later revision v3 failed on items 41–60; the owner now calibrates v3's revision v4 on items 1–20, which are new relative to v3's failed calibration.
scenario.when: The scorer is asked to score a judgment task whose calibration record for v4 names items 1–20.

ground.reason: ACE-A67 requires the scorer, run twice over unchanged inputs, to write nothing, while ACE-A49 and the traceability table make the scorer's report a first-class artifact that states pooled rates and names unlocked cases. The set never says whether that report is a persisted artifact; the decision is significant because the repository's own pattern (ACE-D8) is to commit run artifacts, and each reading yields a different verdict on ACE-A67.

objections.objection: The wording leaves open whether the scorer's report is written to disk: if it is persisted (the reading ACE-D8's commit-everything stance and the traceability table's 'scorer report' check suggest), every scoring run violates ACE-A67's write-nothing clause; if it is stdout-only, ACE-A67 passes but the traceability column has no artifact to point at.

scenario.expect: Under a persisted-report implementation the second run writes the report and fails ACE-A67; under a stdout-only implementation it passes ACE-A67 but no committed scorer report exists for the traceability table's 'scorer report' check to read.
scenario.given: A completed attempt with committed reports and a scorer whose report under ACE-A49 states each lens's pooled rates and names every unlocked case.
scenario.when: The scorer is run twice over the unchanged attempt, as ACE-A67's idempotence check requires.

ground.reason: ACE-D8 and ACE-A21 block a new attempt only while a planned attempt has no committed reports. An attempt that fails partway, with some reports committed and the rest never produced, is neither scored (ACE-A53 refuses it for not matching planned runs one to one) nor blocking (it has committed reports). The failure path of an abandoned, partially committed attempt is untested and the refusal condition as written does not cover it.

objections.objection: The criteria let a partially committed attempt leave its cases pending forever while the planner permits fresh attempts, so the evaluation of record silently stalls on cases that can neither score nor be re-planned.

scenario.expect: refusal naming the still-open attempt, which the document implies is the intent of the serialization rule, but which no criterion tests because ACE-A21's refusal triggers only when the planned attempt has no committed reports at all
scenario.given: A planned attempt in which reports for some planned runs are committed under evals/runs/<run-id>/ and the remaining runs were never dispatched or produced no usable report
scenario.when: the planner is asked to plan a new attempt

ground.reason: ACE-A53's response-ID collision check is scoped to one attempt. When a prompt change alters a fingerprint, a new attempt on the same case is legal, and nothing checks that its reports' response IDs were not already seen in earlier committed attempts. The repeated-run case across attempt boundaries is untested.

objections.objection: The criteria let a replayed report from a superseded attempt pass the collision check inside a later attempt, so a run that never happened under the current fingerprint can count toward a lock.

scenario.expect: refusal naming the reused response ID, since the same transport response cannot evidence two distinct planned runs, which no criterion checks because ACE-A53 compares response IDs only within the attempt being scored
scenario.given: A committed earlier attempt on case C1 and a new attempt on C1 under a changed fingerprint, into which a report from the earlier attempt is filed with its original response ID
scenario.when: the scorer validates the new attempt's reports
